Comprehension:
Read the passage and answer the following questions.

In recent years, urban farming has gained attention as a sustainable way to address food insecurity in cities. Rooftops, balconies, and vacant plots are being converted into small vegetable gardens where residents grow leafy greens, tomatoes, herbs, and even fruits. This trend is not limited to individuals; several residential societies now encourage collective farming projects, allowing neighbours to share produce and responsibilities.
Urban farming also promotes environmental benefits. Plants help reduce heat in concrete-heavy neighbourhoods and improve air quality. Residents who participate in these activities report feeling more connected to nature despite living in crowded urban settings. However, urban farming also comes with challenges such as limited sunlight, water availability, and maintenance of soil quality. Still, the movement continues to grow because it offers more than just food. It fosters collaboration, encourages healthy eating habits, and transforms unused spaces into green, productive patches.
Which real-world issue does the passage connect to?

Urban farming guarantees high crop yield
